And on the eighth day and beyond, it will be accepted unto gifts a fruit-offering to the Lord, and a calf and a sheep, it and its child you will not slaughter in one day.’ So then he does not allow to slaughter a lamb newly-born and still under-breast, showing that the still incomplete and as in understanding short and weak is not yet sacred; and still unacceptable on account of this to God. Such some were both unwise and small-knowing, toward whom all-divine Paul writes: ‘For also owing to be teachers through the time, again you have need of the one teaching you what are the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have become having need of milk, not of solid food; and the solid food is of perfect ones.’ So then still incomplete is the in milk and under breast, according at least to the in understanding I mean and spiritual stoutness; and let the word concerning these go for us again, as from a type of the things in sense and clear, upon the things beyond sense and intelligible, yet that all things have come to be in Christ and in perfection and acceptance, you will understand very well. For the animals being brought forward and dedicated to God, he says must be seven days under the mother, and on the eighth day and beyond, will be a gift, and unto a fruit-offering to God.
Palladius: The word is not very clear.
Cyril: Or do you not say that the eighth is the resurrection day of the Savior, and as a beginning of a new age, with the according to law as in the first seven days having ridden past?
Palladius: I say.

Cyril: So then still unsacred and not-to-be-brought-forward is the as in time the according to the law clearly the in fleshly worship; and already a gift and well-acceptable to God is every thing remaining in Christ according to the eighth and beyond. For unceasing is the calling in Christ, having beginning the resurrection. And knowing this the Son himself was saying, sometimes, ‘When I am lifted up from the earth, I will drag all toward myself,’ and sometimes, ‘Amen I say to you, unless the grain having fallen into the earth should die, it remains alone; and if it should die, it bears more fruit.’
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly. And the not needing to be destroyed-together
notes_covered: Exod 23 / Lev 22 milk and eighth day
translator_notes: Ends mid into §28 mother/children one day.

title: Mother not killed with young = Jerusalem spared; no grove by altar = no pagan décor
english: Palladius: …needing mother with the children in one day, what again would it be?

Cyril: Having legislated very well the things upon Christ, and having announced beforehand gracefully the perfection through him, he has not been ignorant, as God, of the unpersuaded of the Jews, and of Jerusalem’s hard-to-rein, and that on account of this cause those from Israel will be destroyed as Lord-killers, and having behaved drunkenly savagely unto the Son, yet Jerusalem will not go away entirely root-and-all, but will remain as desolate of children, awaiting the last and in ends time, according to which she herself also will be saved running behind the nations; for she has been set unto a back—that is, behind—according to the Psalmist’s voice, ‘Because he will set them a back’; for all Israel will be saved, with the flock from nations having been folded beforehand in the divine pens. So then the law does not allow the corruption as in a last total-destruction to come to be, announcing beforehand the anger upon the unpersuaded mixed with gentleness, and at the same time, I think, setting the matter as some types of necessary knowledge. For least of all will the beings go away unto nothing being tyrannized by unmixed corruption, but this will remain as in successions in that, and that perhaps in this being saved, according at least to the same-race or same-form, God driving away the utter destruction of his own creatures. ‘For he created unto being all things and saving are the begettings of the world,’ according to what has been written. And the fore-announcement of such things was also fitting, and indeed also the showing, of the words concerning Christ, through whom and in whom the things corrupted are saved, and what is tyrannized by death has bloomed again unto life, for the root of the human race has died as some mother, as in Adam, yet those from her—that is, we—have bloomed again in Christ and we are and are saved, having him as life and as a second root of the race.
Palladius: How well indeed and very polished the word holds.

Cyril: And it is worthy, O Palladius, to bring upon the things said: ‘You will not plant for yourself a grove; every tree beside the altar of Lord your God, you will not make for yourself, you will not set for yourself a pillar, which Lord your God has hated.’ For see how he wholly houses-out the worshipper of the truth from idol-fitting deceit, least of all allowing to use up the laws of Greeks, and charging that the customs beside those must be shaken off, even if they should have nothing grieving, and if they should perhaps come to be.
Palladius: What sort of thing do you say?

Cyril: Greeks taking all the most well-branching of plants and thickly leafy occupying a thicket were setting altars and sacrifices to the demons. For it was necessary, necessary that as it were a carrying-away of mind, and indeed also worldly delights, have been fixed beside the altars of the demons. For the false is sick from home with the weak, and is often beautified with the imported adornments,
translator_notes: Ends mid into §29 women’s adornment comparison.

title: Truth’s altar needs no pagan cosmetics; princes’ wagons/oxen; Judah’s first gift
english: Cyril: …just as indeed also the unseemly things of the women. And for the divine altar flashing with the beauty of the truth, of what outside helps, or random adornments, was there need? For the divine is not approachable through worldly delight, nor with a mind somehow relaxed and kindling toward the fleshly things, but as in a sober understanding and looking much toward the above and in heavens. If entirely there was also under trunks perhaps, as having come to be from itself somewhere a divine altar, the matter would have wronged nothing the firm and genuine worshipper of the Savior; but since the practice is entirely Greek, the imitation must be declined, and the resembling of the custom, just as indeed, for the faithful and stood mind toward true knowledge, there is no idol in world, nor is there an idol-sacrifice, yet to eat is not allowed, another charging through the conscience of the weaker; ‘For why am I judged by another conscience? If I share by grace, why am I blasphemed, for what I give thanks?’ So then the matter is well-reputed beside God—I mean to decline the same-working toward Greeks, as both in the setting of the altars, and in the customs and manners concerning religion.
Palladius: I agree.

Cyril: And that one must fruit-bear unto glory of God, and not go into the holy tent having empty hands, the sacred Letter was clarifying again for us, holding thus in the Numbers: ‘And it came to be, on which day Moses finished, so as to raise the tent, and he anointed it, and sanctified it, and all its vessels, and the altar, and all its vessels, and he anointed them, and sanctified them. And the rulers of Israel brought forward, twelve rulers of houses of their families… And they brought their gift opposite Lord, six covered wagons, and twelve oxen, a wagon from two rulers, and a calf from each. And they brought forward opposite the tent. And Lord said toward Moses, saying: Take from them, and they will be toward the liturgical works of the tent of the testimony, and you will give them to the Levites each according to his liturgy.’ And not as far as these were the things from the tribe-rulers; and other things have also been brought forward in addition. For it has been written, ‘And the rulers brought forward unto the inauguration of the altar, on the day on which he anointed it… And Lord said toward Moses: One ruler according to day, a ruler according to day will bring forward their gifts unto the inauguration of the altar. And the one bringing forward on the first day his gift was Naasson son of Aminadab, ruler of the tribe of Judah. And he brought forward his gift, one silver bowl, one hundred thirty its weight; one silver bowl, seventy shekels according to the holy shekel.
translator_notes: Ends mid Judah gift inventory into §30.

title: Twelve-day gifts = Christ offered daily; calf/ram/lamb/goat types; Church rests on Christ
english: Cyril: …both full of fine flour having been mixed in oil unto sacrifice, one spoon of ten golds, full of incense, one calf from cattle, one ram, one yearling lamb unto whole-burnt-offering. And one kid from goats concerning sin; and unto a sacrifice of salvation two heifers, five rams, five he-goats, five yearling ewe-lambs. This gift of Naasson son of Aminadab.’ And they were also bringing forward in succession as far as the twelfth, according at least to the equal manner and in indistinguishable ambitions, each one’s specifically arranged day having been distributed; for God was typing thus.
Palladius: And what then is the word of the thus many-formed bringing-forward?

Cyril: So then the matter is fruit-bearing, O Palladius, and a mystical word has also been woven for it, I think, carrying the riddle up unto Emmanuel, and unto us ourselves; and I will speak again as I am able. For when the holy and true tent has been shown in this world—that is, the Church—Christ conspicuous in it many-formedly and all but from us and for us is brought forward as a sacred victim to God and Father, a ransom and exchange of the life of all, one worth-all. For when the Only-begotten has become human as one from us, he has brought himself forward to God and Father, as some firstfruit and firstling of the human nature fragrant in sanctification, existing naturally and essentially, according as he is thought and is God, and again having been mixed in through the human. And being one also himself, he was being written according to many manners, as at least in the bringing-forward of the rulers, and Christ is as it were also now being sacrificed, being thought many-manneredly through the leaders according to times, and having been honored with differing names; and a bringing-forward according to day, the matter hinting the as-it-were unfailing and unceasing of Christ’s sacrifice in every day and the fruit-bearing in it of those justified in faith. For the worshippers will not fail, nor will there be scarcity of gift-bearing; and Christ will be brought forward toward us and for us, being sacrificed mystically in the holy tents. And he himself is our first and exceptional fruit-bearing; for he has brought himself forward unto sacrifice to the Father, and not rather for himself, according to the word holding blamelessly, but for us under yoke and writing of sin. And according to likeness the toward him, we also are sacred victims, dying to world, as sin has been put-to-death in us, and living to God, the life in sanctification and holiness. For these things the bringing-forward of the rulers seems to hint for us, which also examining part by part with the fitting reasonings, how it would hold well for us, do you wish we say according to what is possible?
Palladius: And very much.
Cyril: So then a calf has been brought forward from each; and the wagons, being six in number, have been distributed to the sacred works of the holy tent. Then from
translator_notes: Ends mid into §31 silver vessels / fine flour.
